result.markdown: --- title: "Session 5 — Choosing, Checking and Reporting" subtitle: "Decision guide · diagnostics · few clusters · sample size for cluster trials · reporting · Lab 5" author: "Community Medicine Workshop" format: revealjs: theme: serif css: [../assets/slide_deck.css, assets/workshop.css, assets/quiz.css] include-after-body: assets/quiz-include.html embed-resources: true slide-number: true navigation-mode: linear code-copy: true center: false transition: fade width: 1280 height: 720 fig-align: center html-math-method: plain execute: echo: true warning: false message: false fig-width: 9 fig-height: 4.6 fig-dpi: 100 --- ## Where we are ::: {.incremental} - Sessions 1 to 4: ICC, design effect, robust SEs, GEE, mixed models, repeated measures - Today: **which one to use**, how to **check** it, how to **plan** a cluster trial and how to **report** it ::: # Topic 1 — Choosing {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Decision guide | Situation | Suggested approach | |---|---| | Few clusters (below about 10) | **Cluster-level** analysis (means, permutation); avoid model-based | | 10 to 40 clusters | **Mixed model** with Satterthwaite/Kenward-Roger df, or **CR2** | | Many clusters, marginal effect wanted | **GEE** or cluster-robust `glm` | | Cluster effects of interest, predictions | **Mixed model** | | Repeated measures, missing visits | **Mixed model** (MAR) | | Binary outcome, population-averaged OR | **GEE** | | Binary outcome, within-cluster OR | **Mixed logistic** (`glmer`) | ## One table of the approaches ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} m_lm <- lm(sbp ~ arm + age + sex + bmi, data = bp12) m_mx <- lmer(sbp ~ arm + age + sex + bmi + (1 | village), data = bp12) tibble(method = c("naive lm", "cluster-robust lm", "mixed model"), estimate = c(coef(m_lm)[["armProgramme"]], coef(m_lm)[["armProgramme"]], fixef(m_mx)[["armProgramme"]]), se = c(summary(m_lm)$coefficients["armProgramme", 2], coeftest(m_lm, vcov = vcovCL(m_lm, cluster = bp12$village))["armProgramme", 2], summary(m_mx)$coefficients["armProgramme", 2])) |> mutate(across(where(is.numeric), \(x) round(x, 2))) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` # A tibble: 3 × 3 method estimate se 1 naive lm -3.42 1.15 2 cluster-robust lm -3.42 1.59 3 mixed model -3.57 1.6 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.key} Report the **honest SE** (cluster-robust or mixed). If someone shows you a clustered analysis with the **naive SE** of 1.15, the result looks **more significant than it is**. ::: # Topic 2 — Checking {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Residuals and random effects ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} par(mfrow = c(1, 2)) qqnorm(ranef(m_mx)$village[, 1], main = "Village effects"); qqline(ranef(m_mx)$village[, 1]) plot(fitted(m_mx), resid(m_mx), xlab = "Fitted", ylab = "Residual", main = "Residuals"); abline(h = 0, col = "red") ``` ::: {.cell-output-display} ![](s5_choose_check_report_files/figure-revealjs/unnamed-chunk-3-1.png){width=900} ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - **Village effects** roughly on the line: normality is plausible. With 40 villages the check is rough - **Residuals**: even band, no funnel - Mixed models are **fairly robust** to the shape of random effects; they are **not** robust to wrong **mean** or **correlation** structures ::: ## Common problems ::: {.warn} - **Singular fit** or non-convergence: too complex (random slopes with few visits): **simplify** - **Few clusters**: SEs and df unreliable - **Cluster-level covariates** with few clusters: low power whatever the number of people - **Treating repeated measures as independent**: the commonest mistake ::: # Topic 3 — Planning and reporting {background-color="#2C3E50"} ## Sample size for a cluster trial ::: {.eq} n~cluster~ = n~individual~ × [ 1 + (m − 1) × ICC ] ::: ::: {.cell} ```{.r .cell-code} 300 * (1 + (25 - 1) * 0.07) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 804 ``` ::: ```{.r .cell-code} ceiling(804 / 25) ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-stdout} ``` [1] 33 ``` ::: ::: ::: {.incremental} - 300 per arm if individually randomised, **25 per village**, ICC 0.07: about **804 people** (**33 villages**) per arm - More **people per village** gives **diminishing returns**; more **villages** helps more - Take the ICC from **earlier studies** and test a range ::: ## Reporting a clustered analysis ::: {.good} - Follow the **CONSORT extension for cluster trials**: number of clusters per arm, mean cluster size, **ICC** - State **how clustering was handled** (mixed model, GEE, cluster-robust, cluster means) - Give **effect, 95% CI**, and the **df method** if few clusters - Say whether the effect is **conditional or marginal** for binary outcomes - Describe how **missing visits** were handled ::: ::: {.key} *Example:* "At 12 months, the programme lowered SBP by 3.6 mmHg (95% CI −6.7 to −0.4), estimated with a linear mixed model with a random intercept for village (40 villages; ICC 0.06)." ::: ## 🔧 Switch to R — Lab 5 {.lab-slide background-color="#1565c0"} ::: {.lab-box} **File:** `clustered-workshop/labs/lab5_report.R` - compare the approaches in one table - sample size for a cluster trial - model checks and a one-sentence result ::: **Time:** 35 minutes · answer the Q questions in the comments ## Self-check quiz (1/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="c5q1" data-type="mcq" data-hash="dyiq94.jstiz3" data-show="QW5hbHlzZSB0aGUgdmlsbGFnZSBtZWFucywgZm9yIGV4YW1wbGUgd2l0aCBhIHBlcm11dGF0 aW9uIHRlc3QgYmV0d2VlbiBhcm1z" data-explain="V2l0aCB2ZXJ5IGZldyBjbHVzdGVycywgcm9idXN0IFNFcyBhbmQgbW9kZWwtYmFzZWQgZGYg YXJlIHVucmVsaWFibGUuIEFuYWx5c2luZyBjbHVzdGVyLWxldmVsIHN1bW1hcmllcyBvciB1 c2luZyBwZXJtdXRhdGlvbiBtZXRob2RzIGtlZXBzIHRoZSB0eXBlIEkgZXJyb3IgcmlnaHQu "} You have 8 villages in a cluster-randomised trial. What is the safest approach? - Fit a cluster-robust lm and report its standard errors without a correction - Treat the 160 adults as independent observations after adjusting for age - Use a GEE with an unstructured working correlation matrix and robust SEs - Analyse the village means, for example with a permutation test between arms ::: ## Self-check quiz (2/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="c5q2" data-type="mcq" data-hash="dyj3hq.jstxgd" data-show="RXh0cmEgcGVvcGxlIGluIGEgdmlsbGFnZSBhZGQgbGl0dGxlLCBzaW5jZSB0aGV5IHNoYXJl IGl0cyBpbmZvcm1hdGlvbg==" data-explain="VGhlIGluZm9ybWF0aW9uIHdpdGhpbiBhIHZpbGxhZ2UgaXMgbGltaXRlZCBieSB0aGUgSUND LiBPbmNlIGNsdXN0ZXJzIGFyZSBsYXJnZSwgZXh0cmEgcGVvcGxlIGFkZCBsaXR0bGUgcHJl Y2lzaW9uLCB3aGlsZSBhIG5ldyB2aWxsYWdlIGFkZHMgaW5kZXBlbmRlbnQgaW5mb3JtYXRp b24u"} Why does adding more people per village help less than adding more villages? - Extra people in a village add little, since they share its information - Villages contain more information than the individual people who live in them - Increasing the number of people per village raises the ICC in a linear way - Extra people can be used in a GEE, but a mixed model cannot use them ::: ## Self-check quiz (3/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="c5q3" data-type="mcq" data-hash="dyjgqh.jsubxs" data-show="QWJvdXQgNzgw" data-explain="REVGRiA9IDEgKyAxOSB4IDAuMDUgPSAxLjk1LCBzbyA0MDAgeCAxLjk1ID0gNzgwIHBlciBh cm0sIG9yIGFib3V0IDM5IGNsdXN0ZXJzIHBlciBhcm0u"} A trial needs 400 per arm if individually randomised. With 20 per cluster and ICC 0.05, about how many per arm are needed? - About 400 - About 420 - About 780 - About 8,000 ::: ## Self-check quiz (4/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="c5q4" data-type="mcq" data-hash="dyjtz5.jsuqf4" data-show="VGhlIG51bWJlciBvZiBjbHVzdGVycyBwZXIgYXJtLCB0aGUgY2x1c3RlciBzaXplcyBhbmQg dGhlIElDQw==" data-explain="VGhlIGV4dGVuc2lvbiBhc2tzIGZvciB0aGUgbnVtYmVyIGFuZCBzaXplIG9mIGNsdXN0ZXJz LCB0aGUgSUNDLCBhbmQgYSBkZXNjcmlwdGlvbiBvZiBob3cgY2x1c3RlcmluZyB3YXMgYWNj b3VudGVkIGZvciBpbiB0aGUgYW5hbHlzaXMu"} Which information should a cluster-randomised trial report according to CONSORT for cluster trials? - The total number of people who took part in the whole trial - The number of clusters per arm, the cluster sizes and the ICC - The p-value of the random intercept test, reported on its own - The names of the villages that were put in each of the arms ::: ## Self-check quiz (5/5) {.smaller} ::: {.quiz-q data-qid="c5q5" data-type="mcq" data-hash="dyk77v.jsv4wi" data-show="VHJlYXRpbmcgdmlzaXRzIGFzIGluZGVwZW5kZW50IG9ic2VydmF0aW9ucyBpbiBhIHJlZ3Jl c3Npb24gbW9kZWw=" data-explain="QW5hbHlzaW5nIGV2ZXJ5IHZpc2l0IGFzIGFuIGluZGVwZW5kZW50IHJvdyBpZ25vcmVzIHRo ZSBjb3JyZWxhdGlvbiB3aXRoaW4gYSBwZXJzb24gYW5kIGdpdmVzIFNFcyB0aGF0IGFyZSB0 b28gc21hbGwgZm9yIGJldHdlZW4tcGVyc29uIGVmZmVjdHMu"} Which mistake is the most common with repeated measures data? - Using a model with a random intercept for each person followed in the study - Plotting the mean trajectory of each group against time since baseline - Treating visits as independent observations in a regression model - Keeping the data in long format, with one row for each visit made ::: ## Score and take-home **Your score: ** ::: {.incremental} - **Few clusters** → cluster-level analysis or small-sample corrections - Check **residuals** and **random effects**; simplify if singular - **Sample size** = individual n × DEFF; **more clusters** beat bigger clusters - Report **clusters, cluster size, ICC**, the method and the **CI** - Never treat repeated measures as independent ::: **Next:** Cheat sheet and the next module

<script>
  // htmlwidgets need to know to resize themselves when slides are shown/hidden.
  // Fire the "slideenter" event (handled by htmlwidgets.js) when the current
  // slide changes (different for each slide format).
  (function () {
    // dispatch for htmlwidgets
    function fireSlideEnter() {
      const event = window.document.createEvent("Event");
      event.initEvent("slideenter", true, true);
      window.document.dispatchEvent(event);
    }

    function fireSlideChanged(previousSlide, currentSlide) {
      fireSlideEnter();

      // dispatch for shiny
      if (window.jQuery) {
        if (previousSlide) {
          window.jQuery(previousSlide).trigger("hidden");
        }
        if (currentSlide) {
          window.jQuery(currentSlide).trigger("shown");
        }
      }
    }

    // hookup for slidy
    if (window.w3c_slidy) {
      window.w3c_slidy.add_observer(function (slide_num) {
        // slide_num starts at position 1
        fireSlideChanged(null, w3c_slidy.slides[slide_num - 1]);
      });
    }

  })();
</script>
